headline: Last short shakeout before travel — legs sharp, HR barely lifting. A week out from the crossing, the taper is complete. From here it's logistics, not fitness.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: Today's run was the shortest and easiest of the taper, sitting entirely in the lowest zone with a capped max — exactly the low-cost confirmation you want in the final week, not a training stimulus. This closes a stretch where recent four-week volume actually ran well above the prior block, so the current quiet reads as a deliberate unloading off a genuinely elevated base, not a fade. Strength went to zero in the last few days after holding through most of the taper — a clean call this close to travel. Steps remain strikingly high for a taper, which tells you background time-on-feet hasn't collapsed even as structured running has thinned. The cardio-load status flags "detraining" purely because logged strain has dropped to nothing; against a base this deep and a demonstrated engine, that's a bookkeeping artifact of the taper, not a fitness signal.
sections.trends: The 16-week shape is a real build peaking into a taper, and the year-to-date comparison against last year is emphatic — you're carrying multiples of the running volume you had at this point twelve months ago. That trajectory is precisely what a 580 km self-supported crossing should be built on: durable accumulation rather than a late spike. The recent flattening is the intended top of the curve, not a plateau in fitness.
sections.threshold: Threshold pace and its anchor HR are unchanged from the baseline, holding steady through the whole build — no erosion despite the volume, which is the read you want. For the crossing itself, threshold is almost beside the point; what matters is that it held while durability accumulated. The engine is intact and parked, ready to be spent slowly over many days rather than in a single hard effort.
sections.zones: The per-session shapes across the block tell a coherent taper story: the genuinely hard day was the mid-July session with real Z4 time, and everything since has walked steadily down through Z2-dominant steady runs into today's pure Z1 shakeout. That descent is exactly right for the final week — you don't want any lingering high-intensity residue going into a multi-day effort. The intensity distribution across the whole build was appropriately polarised, with the bulk easy and the sharpness concentrated in a few sessions.
sections.hr_comparison: The most recent strength sessions carry no HR at all, so there's nothing new to read on that front; the earlier strength HR data sat sensibly low, matching functional-fitness work rather than a cardio session. Nothing in the run HR sources looks out of pattern this week — the easy runs are cheap and consistent, with today's the cheapest of the lot.
sections.calendar: The calendar shows the running rhythm deliberately thinning across the final fortnight while strength held on until the very last days, then stopped — a controlled wind-down rather than an abrupt stop. What stands out is that the frequency reduction is asymmetric: running went quiet earlier, strength lingered, and background stepping never dropped. That's a taper managed by intent across modalities, not a single switch flipped.
sections.personal_bests: No PBs are in play this week and none should be — the shorter fast bests belong to a different focus, and the taper is deliberately suppressing anything resembling a hard effort. The relevant benchmark now is your longest-effort durability, and that's exactly what the coming days will test rather than any pace record.

watch_items: Watch how easy-run HR behaves once the crossing begins under pack load and cumulative days — the first sustained days will redefine what "easy" costs.
Note whether steps stay warm through the packing-and-travel window or dip as logistics peak — a proxy for how much incidental movement survives the transition.
Once underway, track back-to-back leg response over the first two or three days — that early durability audit is the real unknown, not fitness.
Keep an eye on whether sleep steadies before travel, given how variable the recent nights have been heading into a demanding effort.
